# orchestrator

Runs ticket work as three levels of Claude Code sessions: triage owns tickets and the plan, a manager per ticket works in its own tmux window or herdr tab and worktree, children in panes beside it. A status band lists them; a guard keeps ticket changes with triage. Needs bun, git, tmux or herdr.

## Install

```bash
magus
```

Find `orchestrator` on the Plugins tab and turn it on. magus registers the `magus`
marketplace if you do not have it, and installs what the plugin needs to actually run —
binaries, MCP servers, CLI tools.

For a team, press `s` to save your plugins as a profile and commit it. Everyone else runs
`magus install` — see [Teams and profiles](../../guides/teams.md).

Prefer to do it by hand? [Installing Magus](../../guides/install.md) has the manual path.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/orchestrator:start-ticket` | Opens a ticket in its own tmux window or herdr tab and worktree, with a manager session started on it, then sets the ticket in progress. |

## Skills

| `orchestrator:child` | Runs this session as a child of a ticket's manager, the bottom of three levels. It does one named part, usually in another repo, asks and reports only to its manager, and leaves closing to i… |
| `orchestrator:manager` | Runs this session as the manager of one ticket, the middle of three levels. It reads the ticket, starts the matching dev workflow, owns the work to release, and runs child sessions for other… |
| `orchestrator:triage` | Runs this session as a product's triage, the top of three levels and the only session that starts, files or rescopes tickets. |
